title: Geometric sequences
competency: Find the common ratio, the nth term and geometric means of a geometric sequence.

keywords.def: A sequence where each term is the previous term times a fixed non-zero number.
The fixed number r: r = next term ÷ this term.
A term m between a and b in a geometric sequence; m = ±√(ab).

en.text: In a geometric sequence you multiply by the same non-zero number every time. That number is the common ratio r = next term ÷ this term. A negative ratio makes the signs alternate.

am.text: በጂኦሜትሪክ ቅደም ተከተል በየጊዜው በአንድ አይነት ዜሮ ያልሆነ ቁጥር እናባዛለን። ይህ ቁጥር የጋራ ሬሾ r ይባላል፤ r = ቀጣዩ ተርም ÷ ይህ ተርም።

screens.title: Not adding this time
screens.after:
Try adding: 6 − 2 = 4 but 18 − 6 = 12. The gaps change, so it is not adding.
Try dividing: 6 ÷ 2 = 3, 18 ÷ 6 = 3, 54 ÷ 18 = 3.
The same ratio each time: we multiply by 3.

screens.title: Find the ratio
items: Ratio −1: −2 ÷ 2 = −1. The sign flips each time.

screens.title: Halving again and again
screens.ask: Tap ▶. Each bar is half of the bar above.
screens.after: 1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8: each term is the one before × 1/2. The common ratio is r = 1/2.

screens.title: Geometric sequence
paras: The ratio between consecutive terms is a non-zero constant.
This constant is the common ratio r.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A sequence where each term is the previous term times a fixed non-zero number.
The fixed number r: r = next term ÷ this term.

screens.text: Find the common ratio r of the geometric sequence 3, 6, 12, 24, 48, …
screens.why:
Step 1: r = next term ÷ this term.
Step 2: 6 ÷ 3 = 2, 12 ÷ 6 = 2, 24 ÷ 12 = 2.
Step 3: the ratio is the same every time.
So r = 2. (1/2 divides the wrong way: 3 ÷ 6.)
screens.clue: Divide a term by the one before it.

screens.ask: Find the next term of the geometric sequence 3, 6, 12, 24, 48, …: the 6th term is ___
screens.why:
Step 1: r = 6 ÷ 3 = 2.
Step 2: 6th term = 5th term × r.
Step 3: 48 × 2 = 96.
So the 6th term is 96. (Trap: 48 + 24 = 72 adds the last gap instead of multiplying.)

screens.ask: Build a geometric sequence from G₁ = 1 and r = 3: G₅ = ___
screens.why:
Step 1: multiply by 3 each time: 1, 3, 9, 27, 81.
Step 2: or use G₅ = G₁ r⁴ = 1 × 3⁴.
Step 3: 3⁴ = 81.
So G₅ = 81.

screens.text: Spot the geometric sequence: which list has the same ratio between every pair of terms?
screens.why:
Step 1: 5, −10, 20, −40: −10 ÷ 5 = −2, 20 ÷ (−10) = −2, −40 ÷ 20 = −2. Constant ratio: geometric.
Step 2: 5, 10, 15, 20: ratios 2, 1.5, … change (it is arithmetic, d = 5).
Step 3: 1, 4, 9, 16 and 2, 3, 5, 8: ratios change.
So the answer is 5, −10, 20, −40, … (a negative r makes the signs flip).
screens.clue: Divide neighbours. Is the answer always the same?

screens.title: Arithmetic, geometric or neither?
screens.why:
Step 1: 4, 8, 16, 32: ratio 2 each time → geometric.
Step 2: 4, 8, 12, 16: gap 4 each time → arithmetic.
Step 3: 1, 4, 9, 16: gaps 3, 5, 7 and ratios 4, 2.25 change → neither.
Step 4: 81, 27, 9, 3: ratio 1/3 → geometric.
Step 5: 7, 7, 7, 7: gap 0 → arithmetic (it is also geometric with r = 1).
screens.clue: Check the gaps and the ratios.
screens.text: Sort each sequence: arithmetic, geometric or neither? Check the gaps and the ratios.

screens.ask: Find the missing term in the geometric sequence 4, ___, 36, 108. The missing term is
screens.why:
Step 1: 36 and 108 are neighbours, so r = 108 ÷ 36 = 3.
Step 2: the missing term is 4 × 3 = 12.
Check: 12 × 3 = 36 ✓.
So the missing term is 12. (20 is the arithmetic middle of 4 and 36, not the geometric one.)
screens.clue: Find r from the last two terms.

ideas.name: The nth term Gₙ = G₁ rⁿ⁻¹

en.text: To reach the nth term, start at G₁ and multiply by r one time fewer than n: Gₙ = G₁ rⁿ⁻¹. From two terms, divide them: the G₁ cancels and you get a power of r. An even power gives two roots, ± .

am.text: n-ኛውን ተርም ለማግኘት ከ G₁ ተነስተን በ r (n − 1) ጊዜ እናባዛለን፤ Gₙ = G₁ rⁿ⁻¹።

screens.title: How many times?
screens.ask: 2, 6, 18, 54, … To get the 4th term from 2, how many times do you multiply by 3?
screens.after:
G₂ = 2 × 3 (once), G₃ = 2 × 3 × 3 (twice), G₄ = 2 × 3 × 3 × 3 (three times).
So to reach term 4 you multiply 3 times: G₄ = 2 × 3³ = 54.
Term n needs n − 1 factors of r.

screens.title: nth term
paras: G₂ = G₁ r.  G₃ = G₁ r².  G₄ = G₁ r³.
Each step gives one more factor r.

screens.title: Explore Gₙ = G₁ rⁿ⁻¹
screens.ask: Move r and n. Watch how fast the terms grow or shrink.
screens.note: Try r = 0.5: the terms get smaller. Try r = −2: the signs flip.

screens.title: The dots of Gₙ = 2ⁿ⁻¹
screens.ask: Tap the dots. Each step right, the height doubles.

points.name: G₅
points.info: 2⁴ = 16. The dots curve upwards: not a line, unlike an arithmetic sequence.

screens.title: Key word
defs: The fixed number r: r = next term ÷ this term.

screens.text: Write the general term of a geometric sequence with G₁ = 3 and r = 2.
screens.why:
Step 1: use Gₙ = G₁ rⁿ⁻¹.
Step 2: put G₁ = 3 and r = 2: Gₙ = 3 × 2ⁿ⁻¹.
Check n = 2: 3 × 2 = 6 ✓.
(Trap: 6ⁿ⁻¹ is wrong. 3 × 2ⁿ⁻¹ is not (3 × 2)ⁿ⁻¹.)
screens.clue: Put G₁ and r into the formula.

screens.text: Write the nth term of the geometric sequence 1, −2, 4, −8, 16, …
screens.why:
Step 1: G₁ = 1 and r = −2 ÷ 1 = −2.
Step 2: Gₙ = 1 × (−2)ⁿ⁻¹ = (−2)ⁿ⁻¹.
Check n = 2: (−2)¹ = −2 ✓; n = 3: (−2)² = 4 ✓.
(−2ⁿ⁻¹ means −(2ⁿ⁻¹): always negative. Keep −2 in brackets.)
screens.clue: r is negative. Keep it in brackets.

screens.ask: Use Gₙ = G₁ rⁿ⁻¹ with G₁ = −3 and r = −1/2: G₅ = ___
screens.why:
Step 1: G₅ = G₁ r⁴ = −3 × (−1/2)⁴.
Step 2: (−1/2)⁴ = (−1)⁴/2⁴ = 1/16. An even power is positive.
Step 3: −3 × 1/16 = −3/16.
So G₅ = −3/16. (Trap: +3/16 forgets that G₁ is negative.)
screens.clue: Work out (−1/2)⁴ first. An even power is positive.

screens.text: Write the nth term of the geometric sequence 27, 9, 3, 1, …
screens.why:
Step 1: r = 9 ÷ 27 = 1/3.
Step 2: Gₙ = 27(1/3)ⁿ⁻¹.
Check n = 4: 27 × 1/27 = 1 ✓.
(27 − 6(n − 1) is arithmetic: it fails at n = 3. 27 × 3ⁿ⁻¹ grows.)

screens.text: Find r from two terms: G₂ = 12 and G₆ = 192. Which values of r are possible?
screens.why:
Step 1: G₆ = G₂ r⁴ (4 steps from term 2 to term 6).
Step 2: r⁴ = 192 ÷ 12 = 16.
Step 3: 2⁴ = 16 and (−2)⁴ = 16.
So r = 2 or r = −2. (16 is r⁴, not r; 4 gives 4⁴ = 256.)
screens.clue: Divide G₆ by G₂. An even power has two roots.

screens.ask: Find a far term from two terms: G₂ = 12, G₆ = 192 and r > 0. G₁₁ = ___
screens.why:
Step 1: r⁴ = 192 ÷ 12 = 16, and r > 0, so r = 2.
Step 2: term 2 to term 11 is 9 steps: G₁₁ = G₂ r⁹.
Step 3: 2⁹ = 512, and 12 × 512 = 6144.
So G₁₁ = 6144.
screens.clue: From term 2 to term 11 is 9 steps.

screens.ask: Find G₁ from two terms: a geometric sequence has G₃ = 18 and G₆ = −486. G₁ = ___
screens.why:
Step 1: G₆ = G₃ r³, so r³ = −486 ÷ 18 = −27.
Step 2: an odd power has one real root: r = −3.
Step 3: G₃ = G₁ r², so G₁ = 18 ÷ (−3)² = 18 ÷ 9 = 2.
Check: 2, −6, 18, −54, 162, −486 ✓.
screens.clue: Divide to get r³. An odd power has one real root.

en.text: If a, m, b are in a geometric sequence, m is a geometric mean of a and b. Equal ratios m/a = b/m give m² = ab, so m = ±√(ab). For three terms with a known product, write them as a/r, a, ar: the r cancels in the product.

am.text: a, m, b ጂኦሜትሪክ ቅደም ተከተል ከሆኑ m የ a እና b ጂኦሜትሪክ አማካይ ነው። m² = ab ስለሆነ m = ±√(ab)።

screens.title: The middle of 2 and 8
screens.ask: 2, m, 8 is geometric. Which m works?
screens.after:
Geometric means equal ratios: m/2 = 8/m, so m² = 16.
2, 4, 8 has ratio 2. Also 2, −4, 8 has ratio −2. So m = ±4.
(5 is halfway: the arithmetic mean, not the geometric one.)

screens.title: Geometric mean
paras: If a, m, b are terms in a geometric sequence, m is the geometric mean.
r = m/a = b/m, so m² = ab.

screens.title: Two kinds of mean
screens.ask: Move a and b. Compare the geometric mean with the arithmetic mean.
screens.note: For positive a and b, √(ab) is never bigger than (a + b)/2. They are equal only when a = b.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A term m between a and b in a geometric sequence; m = ±√(ab).

screens.text: Find the geometric mean between 3 and 12.
screens.why:
Step 1: 3, m, 12 has equal ratios: m/3 = 12/m.
Step 2: m² = 3 × 12 = 36.
Step 3: m = ±6.
Check: 3, 6, 12 (r = 2) and 3, −6, 12 (r = −2) ✓.
(7.5 is the arithmetic mean; ±36 forgets the square root.)

screens.text: Arithmetic mean or geometric mean? True or false: the geometric mean of 4 and 9 is 6.5.
screens.why:
Step 1: 6.5 = (4 + 9)/2 is the arithmetic mean.
Step 2: the geometric mean uses m² = ab = 4 × 9 = 36.
Step 3: m = ±√36 = ±6.
So the statement is false.
screens.clue: Multiply, then take the square root.

screens.title: Three terms: sum 35, product 1000
steps: Let them be a/r, a, ar. Product = a³ = 1000, so a = 10.

screens.ask: Use equal ratios: x, 4x + 3, 7x + 6 are geometric, x ≠ 0. x = ___
screens.why:
Step 1: equal ratios: (4x + 3)/x = (7x + 6)/(4x + 3).
Step 2: cross-multiply: (4x + 3)² = x(7x + 6).
Step 3: 16x² + 24x + 9 = 7x² + 6x, so 9x² + 18x + 9 = 0.
Step 4: divide by 9: x² + 2x + 1 = (x + 1)² = 0, so x = −1.
Check: −1, −1, −1 has r = 1 ✓.

screens.ask: Find the positive geometric mean of 5 and 45: ___
screens.why:
Step 1: m² = 5 × 45 = 225.
Step 2: m = √225 = 15 (positive root).
Check: 5, 15, 45 has ratio 3 ✓.
(25 is the arithmetic mean.)

screens.ask: Three geometric terms have product 216 and sum 21. Find the middle term: ___
screens.why:
Step 1: write the terms as a/r, a, ar.
Step 2: product: (a/r) × a × ar = a³ = 216, so a = 6.
Step 3: sum: 6/r + 6 + 6r = 21 gives 2r² − 5r + 2 = 0, so r = 2 or 1/2.
The terms are 3, 6, 12, and the middle term is 6.
screens.clue: Write the terms as a/r, a, ar.

items.ask: Find the next term of the geometric sequence 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, …: the 6th term is ___
items.why:
Step 1: r = 2 ÷ 1 = 2.
Step 2: 6th term = 16 × 2 = 32.
Check: G₆ = 1 × 2⁵ = 32 ✓.

items.text: Build a geometric sequence from G₁ = 1 and r = 3: which are terms 2 to 5?
items.why:
Step 1: multiply by r = 3 each time.
Step 2: 1 × 3 = 3, 3 × 3 = 9, 9 × 3 = 27, 27 × 3 = 81.
So the terms are 3, 9, 27, 81.
(4, 7, 10, 13 adds 3: that is arithmetic.)
items.clue: r is a ratio, not a difference.

items.text: Write the general term of a geometric sequence with G₁ = 2 and r = 5: Gₙ =
items.why:
Step 1: Gₙ = G₁ rⁿ⁻¹.
Step 2: Gₙ = 2 × 5ⁿ⁻¹.
Check n = 1: 2 × 5⁰ = 2 ✓. (2 × 5ⁿ gives G₁ = 10.)

items.text: Write the general term of a geometric sequence with G₁ = 2 and r = −2: Gₙ =
items.why:
Step 1: Gₙ = G₁ rⁿ⁻¹ = 2(−2)ⁿ⁻¹.
Step 2: keep −2 in brackets so the sign alternates.
Check: n = 1, 2, 3 gives 2, −4, 8 ✓.
(−2(2)ⁿ⁻¹ is always negative.)

items.text: Write the nth term of the geometric sequence 3/2, 3/4, 3/8, 3/16, …: Gₙ =

items.ask: Use Gₙ = G₁ rⁿ⁻¹ with G₁ = −3 and r = −1/2: G₅ = ___
items.why:
Step 1: G₅ = −3 × (−1/2)⁴.
Step 2: (−1/2)⁴ = 1/16 (even power, positive).
Step 3: −3 × 1/16 = −3/16.
So G₅ = −3/16.

items.text: Find the geometric mean between 3 and 12.
items.why:
Step 1: m² = 3 × 12 = 36.
Step 2: m = ±6.
Both work: 3, 6, 12 (r = 2) and 3, −6, 12 (r = −2).
("6 only" misses the negative root.)

items.text: Use two terms to find a far term: G₂ = 12 and G₆ = 192. Which values of G₁₁ are possible?
items.why:
Step 1: r⁴ = 192 ÷ 12 = 16, so r = 2 or r = −2.
Step 2: G₁₁ = G₂ r⁹ (9 steps).
Step 3: 2⁹ = 512 and (−2)⁹ = −512 (odd power).
Step 4: G₁₁ = 12 × 512 = 6144 or 12 × (−512) = −6144.

items.ask: Use equal ratios: x, 4x + 3, 7x + 6 are geometric. x = ___

items.text: Three geometric terms have sum 35 and product 1000. Which are they?
items.why:
Step 1: write them as a/r, a, ar. Product a³ = 1000, so a = 10.
Step 2: 10/r + 10 + 10r = 35, so 2r² − 5r + 2 = 0.
Step 3: r = 2 or 1/2: the terms are 5, 10, 20 either way.
Check: 5 + 10 + 20 = 35 and 5 × 10 × 20 = 1000 ✓.
(2, 10, 50: sum 62.)

test.ask: Use Gₙ = G₁ rⁿ⁻¹ with G₁ = 4 and r = 3: G₄ = ___

test.text: Find the common ratio of the geometric sequence 48, −24, 12, −6, …
test.why:
r = next term ÷ this term.
−24 ÷ 48 = −1/2, and 12 ÷ (−24) = −1/2.
The signs flip, so r is negative.
r = −1/2.

test.ask: Find r from two terms: G₁ = 2 and G₄ = 54. r = ___

test.text: Find the geometric mean of 2 and 18.
test.why:
m² = 2 × 18 = 36.
m = ±6.
Check: 2, 6, 18 has ratio 3 ✓.
(10 is the arithmetic mean.)

test.ask: Find G₁ from two terms: G₃ = 20 and G₅ = 80, r > 0. G₁ = ___
test.why:
G₅ = G₃ r², so r² = 80 ÷ 20 = 4.
r > 0, so r = 2.
G₃ = G₁ r², so G₁ = 20 ÷ 4 = 5.
Check: 5, 10, 20, 40, 80 ✓.

notes.text: Exercise 1.9 Q2 has two answers (r = ±2 gives G₁₁ = ±6144); the book expects both.

screens.title: (−1/2)⁴ and (−1/2)³
steps: Any non-zero number to the power 0 is 1.

screens.why:
Step 1: (−3)⁴ = (−3)(−3)(−3)(−3).
Step 2: (−3)(−3) = 9, and 9 × 9 = 81.
Step 3: 4 minus signs pair up, so the result is positive.
So (−3)⁴ = 81. (−81 would be −3⁴ without brackets.)
